title: A sweep draws as a smooth curve with its head along the curve's end
body:
Today `Connector::path` in `crates/acre/src/scene/connector.rs` turns every curve, `sweep` included, into `CURVE_STEPS` (24) straight segments. `draw_shaft` draws them as one `Primitive::Polyline` and aims the head along the last segment. On a long sweep each segment is about 50 px, so the corners show. The last segment cuts across the bend, so a head that should point along the curve's end leans off it, by up to about 25° on a sweep 1200 px wide and 190 px tall.

## Proposal

- A primitive `Primitive::Cubic { from, c1, c2, to, stroke }`. The PNG, SVG and PDF renderers draw it as a Bézier curve, with tiny-skia's `cubic_to`, an SVG `C` path and krilla's path builder.
- `sweep` draws its shaft as one `Cubic`, cut where the head begins by splitting the curve. Its head points along the curve's tangent at the end, which for a sweep is its `enter` way or the reverse of its side's outward direction.
- `Connector::path` still gives the points that bounds and following use.

## Out of scope

- `arrow { route curve; }` keeps its 24 segments. Drawing it through `Cubic` would keep its shape but change its pixels in every figure that uses it, so that waits for Jack.
